shapes.text: The shapes, the catalogue, and the screen we have now

phones.text: The same flow on a phone

why.text:
The rule behind all four screens: never show a consequence of an answer nobody has given.

Today the editor shows a payment method before a price, a "Free" label before anyone said free, and a summary that reads "Nothing is collected" while the card chip is lit. Three claims about one unanswered question.

nothing.text:
Nothing stored changes.

Free is price 0. A set price is price > 0 plus a collection. A quote is sale_mode proposal. Same three rows the database holds today, same publish gates, same requirement rules — only the order they are asked in.

mobile.text:
What changes on a phone, and what does not.

The four questions stay four questions. A step that fits a phone fits a desktop; the reverse is what fails.

The dialog becomes a full-screen sheet — a frame inside a frame wastes the only width there is. The stepper loses its labels and keeps its four dashes, because position says the same thing in a tenth of the space. The client-view rail becomes one line you can open, since it is reassurance rather than input. Side-by-side choices stack. Every action a row offers moves under its text rather than beside it, and nothing hides behind a swipe.

One button, pinned above the home indicator, always the next step. Targets 44px and up; the price field 17px so iOS does not zoom the page when it is focused.
